name: Calcitriol
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 0.25 mcg/day; increase by 0.25 mcg/day every 4 to 8 weeks; most hemodialysis patients respond to 0.5 to 1 mcg/day
Start 0.25 mcg/day; may increase to 0.5 mcg/day

key_interactions.action: Set the calcitriol dose with care; monitor calcium.
Withhold pharmacologic vitamin D doses during calcitriol.
Do not use during calcitriol therapy in dialysis patients.
Adjust the binder dose to serum phosphate.

key_interactions.effect: Lower endogenous 25(OH)D3; calcitriol needs may rise.
key_interactions.action: Higher calcitriol doses may be needed.

common: Label gives no frequencies; adverse effects mirror vitamin D excess (hypercalcemia syndrome)
serious: Vascular and soft-tissue calcification, nephrocalcinosis (chronic hypercalcemia)

contraindications: Hypercalcemia or evidence of vitamin D toxicity
Hypersensitivity to calcitriol, the drug class, or inactive ingredients
monitoring: Serum calcium at least twice weekly during titration, then monthly
Phosphorus, magnesium and alkaline phosphatase periodically
Calcium x phosphate product (keep below 70 mg²/dL²)

pk.peak: 3 to 6 hours (healthy); 8 to 12 hours in hemodialysis patients
pk.half_life: 5 to 8 hours (single oral dose, healthy adults)
pk.half_life_eskd: About 21.9 hours in hemodialysis patients; at least twofold longer in chronic renal failure (label)
pk.protein_binding: About 99.9% bound in blood (vitamin D binding protein)
pk.metabolism: 24-hydroxylation pathway to calcitroic acid; lactone pathway
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 10% of an oral dose in urine at 24 hours; mainly fecal (biliary)
pk.dialyzability: Not stated; hypercalcemia can be corrected by dialysis against calcium-free dialysate (label).

sources.citation: ANI Pharmaceuticals, Inc.. (2026). Calcitriol (calcitriol) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA021068, set ID bdb9c0d4-bdb3-4174-a4d9-55c423f38476, version effective July 10, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: 'Separate or monitor response' for cholestyramine is our wording; the label only states the absorption effect. Consider deleting the action or the row.
Label is the oral solution (ANI, NDA021068); the PH market is mostly capsules.
The 16.2 h / 21.9 h half-lives are reported 'respectively' for nephrotic syndrome and hemodialysis; 21.9 h assigned to hemodialysis.
